campaigns.title: This Ganeshotsav, help PETA India save elephants from captivity and abuse
campaigns.description: At various tourist destinations across the country elephants are worked to exhaustion for tourism and entertainment. They work long hours on concrete that wrecks their feet, legs and joints. Some are visually impaired. Many are underfed, surviving on scraps no wild elephant would eat. Brutally assaulted by their trainers, many work out of force and fear despite grievous injuries. When they are not working, they are restrained in chains. They have no choice, no rest, no freedom.PETA India (People for Ethical Treatment of Animals, India) is on a mission to save these sensitive animals and ease their suffering forever. This is where your support becomes crucial. PETA India is in urgent need of funds to protect these animals from further abuse. Your donation can mean a life of freedom for a captive elephant who has only known a life of pain and giving rides. Donate generously.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).A life of suffering behind the spectacleElephants used for rides and other entertainment are separated from their mothers, often taken from the wild, and then put through months of gruesome training meant only to break them. The training methods employed are immensely violent. Weapons such as ankushes or sharp-tipped sticks may be used to control them, leaving them living under the threat of pain and fear.The suffering does not end there. Years of standing and walking on concrete can cause chronic foot, joint and musculoskeletal problems in captive elephants. Some elephants used for rides have also been documented as visually impaired. Injured or sick elephants commonly continue working, while inadequate food and water can leave them malnourished and dehydrated.Donate to help end the cycle of exploitationPETA India has been on a mission to rescue these sensitive souls and has also been advocating for an end to elephant rides and other use of elephants for entertainment, working to create alternatives, including its mechanical elephant donation programme. Your donation can helpYour support can help PETA India continue its efforts to protect captive elephants from:Cruel training and weaponsHeavy loads and exhaustionChains and confinementStarvation and neglectInjuries and chronic painExploitation for tourism and spectacleHelp save overworked captive elephants from exploitation, chains, weapons and abuse. Donate today and stand for a life of freedom and compassion.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support PETA India, in its mission to free captive elephants from abuse.

campaigns.title: Don’t let children fight cancer on an empty stomach, help them with nutrition. Donate now
campaigns.description: “My 4-year-old son was diagnosed with an aggressive form of leukaemia. We brought him to Mumbai 6 months back when he was fighting for life. But within a couple of months, Vidhan’s condition improved drastically. Apart from the chemotherapy, one thing that has had a significant impact on his health is the nutrition support provided by Cuddles Foundation,” says Meenakshi Motiwala, who hails from Dhule, Maharashtra. Meenakshi and her husband had no means of supporting Vidhan with special nutrition, but thanks to the NGO, their son is in better shape.Cuddles Foundation is a nonprofit that helps hundreds of children fight cancer each year, but there are thousands more still battling cancer and in need of help. Help the NGO extend its reach and save many more lives. Donate now.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India)Non-profit organisation Cuddles Foundation has been on a mission to give underprivileged children having cancer a fighting chance against the disease with complete nutritional support. Giving kids battling cancer a fighting chanceDoctors often say that proper nutrition is the first line of treatment for children fighting cancer. However, because of poor financial background, many parents can’t give their kids life-saving nutrition and often witness the condition deteriorate before their eyes. “We have observed that there is a marked improvement or maintenance in the health and nutritional status of more than 80% of children with cancer by giving them proper meals. Nutritional support can not only give a child the strength needed to go through chemotherapy, but also help in reducing the side effects of cancer treatment significantly. Sadly, the life-saving nutrition needed to help children defeat cancer is well beyond the reach for many parents due to their financial condition,” says Purnota Dutta Bahl, founder of the nonprofit. Purnota embarked upon the mission to save the lives of children with cancer over a decade back after a chance visit to the Tata Memorial Hospital. “I saw a baby girl who back then, was about the same age as my daughter. The girl was fighting cancer and was visibly malnourished. I was informed by the nurse that children get treatment for cancer at the hospital free of cost, but their condition keeps deteriorating as their parents can’t afford the required nutrition. It was on that day that I decided to at least give these children a fighting chance against cancer,” explains the founder of the nonprofit organisation. Donate to heal thousands more“We have been able to take our programme to over 50 hospitals, spread across 17 states. But still there are thousands of children we are yet to reach. The cost of providing nutritional support to a child and their family suffering from cancer is about ₹80,000 per year (or ₹7,000 a month). Cancer is absolutely curable. A little love and support from you can help children suffering from cancer complete their treatment and go on to live functional and productive lives in the future,” says Purnota.Donate to this fundraiser by give.do, India’s largest fundraising platform, to support Cuddles Foundation in their mission to give life-saving nutrition to children suffering from cancer and give them the strength to fight cancer.

campaigns.title: Urgent!! Help the flood-affected people of Bihar
campaigns.description: Bihar is in the grip of one of its worst floods in a decade. Nearly 48 lakh people across 15 districts including Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Madhepura and Araria. People are living through inundated homes, submerged fields and cut-off villages. Around 575 gram panchayats across 87 blocks are under water.Our NGO partner ActionAid is on the ground helping the flood-affected. Help ActionAid deliver ration, hygiene, shelter and education kits to flood-hit families. Donate now.Ravaging floodsIn Bhagalpur, the Ganga river is flowing nearly two metres above the danger mark. The Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Punpun, Bagmati and Ghaghra are all swollen past their danger levels too, and embankment breaches in Bhagalpur have let floodwaters pour into new areas. With more rain forecast, thousands of families who have already lost their homes, food stocks and livelihoods are bracing for the water to rise further.Relief camps are stretched thin, and community kitchens can't keep pace with the need. Families are sheltering on rooftops, embankments and roadsides — with nothing but what they could carry.ActionAid’s action on the groundGive.do has partnered with ActionAid Association, which has decades of on-ground experience in disaster response across Bihar, to reach the worst-affected families with life-saving relief. Here's exactly what your donation will fund:₹1,530 — a Ration Kit, feeding a family for weeks with essentials like rice, dal, oil, salt and spices, when floodwaters have wiped out food stocks and cut off access to markets.₹765 — a Hygiene Kit, with soap, sanitary products, disinfectant and basic medicines, to prevent the disease outbreaks that follow floods when clean water and sanitation collapse.₹1,500 — a Shelter Kit, including tarpaulin sheets and essentials to help a family build temporary shelter after losing their home to the water.Every one of these kits goes directly to a family that has lost almost everything in the last few days. ActionAid's teams are already on the ground in the worst-hit districts, and are scaling up to reach more villages as the water spreads — but they need funds to do it fast.Bihar doesn't need sympathy. It needs food, clean water and shelter.Donate today and help ActionAid reach families in need. Donate to this fundraiser by give.do, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Bihar flood survivors.

campaigns.title: Give Every Child with Cancer and blood disorder a Better Chance to survive
campaigns.description: Hello! My name is Kamna Dogra, and I am a fundraising volunteer with the INPHOG Research Foundation (Indian Pediatric Hematology and Oncology Group).Every year, approximately 75,000 children in India develop cancer and serious blood disorders. Every child deserves the best possible treatment and a chance to live a healthy life.INPHOG is a nationwide network of pediatric oncologists, hematologists, and hospitals working together to improve survival outcomes for children with cancer and blood disorders. Through standardized, evidence-based treatment protocols and collaborative research, INPHOG helps improve treatment and the quality of care for children across India.Your support will help advance research that leads to better treatments and gives more children with cancer and blood disorders a better chance at life.Every donation, no matter the size, can help create a brighter future for children and their families. Thank you for your kindness and support.

campaigns.title: Give a Child in Prayagraj a Full Year of School-Padhega Prayagraj, Badhega Bharat
campaigns.description: Give a Child in Prayagraj a Full Year of SchoolEvery twelve years, Prayagraj hosts the largest human gathering on Earth — millions arrive at the Sangam seeking renewal. A few kilometres away, in the city's urban slums, 853 children are trying to get something smaller and harder to find: a first chance at an education.RAH Foundation runs 3 literacy centers across Prayagraj's urban slum communities. This year, we're asking for ₹35,00,000 to keep every one of those 853 children in school, and to keep the results moving in the right direction.What's already working:Attendance: 42% → 73%Parent engagement in their child's learning: 35% → 63%Hindi learning levels: up 47%Maths learning levels: up 42%These aren't projections. This is what happened after RAH's 3 centers opened and stayed open. The ask now is simple — keep them open, and keep this trajectory going for another year.Our Vision: To inclusive India where every child in an urban slum has access to quality education regardless of where they're born. Our Mission: To close the education gap in underserved urban communities through community based literacy centres that are sustainable and built to scale. Where Your Money Goes₹35,00,000 spread across 853 children works out to ₹4,103 per child, per year. That covers one child's place at a literacy center for a full academic year.Your Gift Impact ₹4,103 One child, fully funded, for one year ₹ 20,515 Five children, one year ₹ 41,030 Ten children, one year ₹ 11,66,667 One center's share of the annual cost ₹ 35,00,000 All 853 children, all 3 centers, one full yearThe AskWe're not asking you to fund a mission statement. We're asking you to fund a seat — a specific one, for a specific child, for a specific year, in a city where a child's chance at school shouldn't depend on which side of the crowd they're born on.Fund one child's year for ₹4,103. Fund ten for ₹41,030. Whatever you give, it goes to one of these 853 kids, not a general fund.Pledge your support, donate now!

campaigns.title: Help abandoned elderly with shelter and care
campaigns.description: Every day, elderly parents are left alone on the streets, at train stations, or even outside temples. Many are sick, struggling with age-related problems, and have no money or family to turn to. Some suffer for weeks or months before anyone notices their pain. The heartbreaking truth? They were abandoned by their own families.Although Indian law requires children and relatives to care for senior citizens, many elders still face neglect, abuse, and abandonment. The problem is only getting worse.But there is hope. Our dedicated NGO partners work day and night to rescue these forgotten elders. They provide safe shelter, medical care, nutritious meals, and most importantly—love and respect. Through old age homes across the country, our partners give these seniors a chance to live their remaining years with dignity, comfort, and peace.You can make a difference. Your donation will help our NGO partners:Rescue homeless elders from the streetsProvide shelter, food, and medical careRestore their faith in humanity with kindness and supportNo elder should spend their final years alone and suffering. Your generosity can give them a fresh start. Donate today and help an abandoned senior citizen find safety, care, and hope.

campaigns.title: Comprehensive Day Care Programmes
campaigns.description: In lieu of better working conditions, a vast majority of the population working in the unorganised sector choose to migrate within the country. Migrants in urban India form a large majority of the work force in the unorganised sectors where they work as construction workers, electricians, plumbers, masons, security personnel, etc. These migrant labourers are usually the most vulnerable and marginalised of the urban poor. Because of the issues like- lack of housing facilities, low wages, expensive housing, overcrowding and a lot more, the migrants are marginalised even further. Children of migrant construction workers are even more vulnerable. Because of the extreme poverty of their families, their parents are constantly working and thus, these children are left to fend for themselves. They suffer from malnutrition, undernourishment, accidents, innumerable health problems and are deprived of formal schooling, day care centres or any sort of support system. MMC adopts a multi-pronged approach to address these issues. We run a comprehensive programme of health, education and nutrition through our day care centres on construction sites to tackle the wide range of issues that surround the children of migrant construction workers.Our comprehensive day care centres-Support the intellectual, emotional and physical development of young children and create the foundations required for mainstreaming them into schools.Help older children enter in schools and perform well by freeing them from the burden of child care.Support the working mothers by reassuring them that her children are safe and looked after.Provide guidance and support to parents on appropriate nutrition, education, health and care, along with several relevant issues of the community.Our vision is for all children to have a nurturing and happy childhood. Our mission is to promote ‘child-friendly sites’; where every child living on a construction site is safe, healthy and educated, and able to enjoy their childhood. MMC aligns with 4 SDGs-No PovertyZero HungerGood Health and Well-beingQuality EducationWe want to create a world where no child is deprived of supportive care, quality education, health and nutrition.
